narrative: Your loan application for 10,623 Deutsche Marks to buy a used car over 30 months was carefully reviewed by our credit model, which predicts the likelihood of repayment issues based on patterns from past borrowers in 1970s Germany. The model estimates a 56% probability that you represent a bad credit risk, meaning it sees a higher-than-even chance of challenges in repaying this loan on time, leading to the denial of your application. The strongest factor pushing toward this concern was the large amount you requested—nearly four times the average of about 2,887 DM sought by approved applicants—which the model views as riskier, especially for someone with your profile including three existing credits at this bank and two financial dependents. Your checking account status, showing a balance below zero, was the next biggest red flag, as this is less common among those approved (only about 20% share this) and signals potential cash flow strain. On a more positive note, your credit history rated as critical or other credits actually worked in your favor, pulling the prediction toward approval since it's a common trait even among half of successful applicants who had existing paid credits. Compared to typical approved applicants—who often request smaller amounts, have healthier checking balances, and fewer existing credits—your situation stands out as higher risk in those key areas. This model doesn't consider factors like your age, gender, or status as a foreign worker, focusing purely on financial indicators. To improve your chances next time, consider requesting a smaller amount, building up your checking account balance, or demonstrating stronger repayment on your current credits first. You might also explore adding a guarantor, as over 90% of approved applicants had none but those who did sometimes tipped the scales. Gathering more savings beyond your current under-100 DM or clarifying property assets could help too. We encourage you to reapply once you've addressed these areas, as many applicants succeed after adjustments.
